Title: \\\"Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: Addressing the Correlation-Selection Gap in Self-Consistency for Named Entity Recognition\\\". **Round 10 critical fixes**: (1) B2 in-domain +3.62pp CONFIRMED LEAKED (train-on-test) — deleted from paper, awaiting out-of-fold re-evaluation; cross-dataset negative transfer valid; (2) P \\\"Impossibility Theorem\\\" downgraded to \\\"Degeneracy Decomposition\\\" — Theorem 1 trivial, Theorem 2 tautological, \\\"information-theoretic\\\" overclaim removed; (3) Ceiling-gap framing retained; (4) MBR v3 retained; (5) FewNERD-primary retained; (6) N Inverse Scaling core finding solid (θ=0.5 immune). Target: Main 4.3+. Scale: 7B→14B→32B→72B Qwen2.5 + 8B cross-family (Qwen3+LLaMA). 14B/32B training in progress.\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 **Main Conference** (via ARR May 2026)\\n- Deadline: ARR May cycle, 2026-05-25\\n\\n## Core Claims (D157 updated — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION: QE + diagnostic + prescriptive)\\n\\n### Claim 1 (PRIMARY — Dual Contribution: QE Framework + Selection Diagnostic)\\n**Positive contribution (A)**: Confidence signals reliably predict structured IE output quality at the population level (AUROC up to 0.82, ρ up to 0.45), enabling practical QE/selective prediction.\\n**Diagnostic contribution (B)** (D154 revised): Selection viability depends on LP signal quality and dataset characteristics, not degeneracy alone:\\n- **Degeneracy as headroom predictor**: High degeneracy eliminates selection headroom (CoNLL 47.4% degen → 0 net gain). Within fixed dataset-model settings, degeneracy causally modulates LP effectiveness (SciERC epoch ablation: −1.18/+0.74/+0.99pp at 3/5/10 epochs; per-entity-type within Few-NERD ρ=−0.881). But across datasets, degeneracy alone does NOT predict LP selection direction (23-point cross-configuration ρ=0.052, p=0.81).\\n- **LP-quality alignment as primary predictor**: LP must track entity-level F1 within instances. Few-NERD within-instance ρ(LP,F1) ≈ 0.5-0.66 → LP selection +1.36pp (p<0.05). SciERC ρ(LP,F1) ≈ 0.18-0.24 → LP fails despite similar degeneracy (17.8% vs 13.8%). This is the primary determinant of LP selection success across datasets.\\n- **Structural signals (SJ/FK/EM/VC)**: universally fail regardless — instance-level aggregates cannot rank candidates by construction.\\n- **Multi-causal diagnosis (D154)**: (1) degeneracy modulates headroom within settings; (2) LP-quality alignment determines cross-dataset selection success; (3) LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy (7.2% vs 17.8%) AND improves LP spread (0.057 vs 0.041 nats) but SciERC's weak LP-F1 alignment (ρ~0.24) still prevents selection success → LP alignment is the binding constraint, degeneracy is a within-setting modulator.\\n\\nThe framing is NOT \\\"selection fails\\\" (pure negative) but \\\"we characterize WHEN LP works (strong LP-F1 alignment), WHY it fails elsewhere (weak alignment + compression), and WHAT distinguishes LP from structural signals\\\" (empirical characterization with diagnostic implications).\\n\\n**Three-layer argument + Capability-diversity tension**:\\n- Layer A (design property, noted not discovered): 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction. This is a conceptual clarification — the \\\"methodological premise\\\" — not an empirical finding.\\n- Layer B (empirical — instance degeneracy): 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom. Within-instance ρ=0.524 (SciERC) and 0.994 (CoNLL) — signals ARE correlated within instances, but degeneracy makes this irrelevant. Non-degenerate instances show MBR closing 23-41% of oracle gap. Selection recovers T=1.0 sampling degradation (LP 0.647 vs Random 0.610, +3.7pp) but only matches T=0 greedy (0.645 macro) at 8× inference cost — zero marginal gain.\\n- Layer C (empirical — LP-quality alignment, revised D123): LP selection requires adequate within-instance correlation with task quality. Few-NERD ρ(LP,F1)≈0.5-0.66 → selection succeeds (+1.36pp). SciERC ρ(LP,F1)≈0.18-0.24 → selection fails even when LP range is adequate (rank=8: 0.057 nats). LP compression (median range 0.041 nats on SciERC full-rank) is a contributing factor but NOT the sole explanation — rank=8 expands LP range to 0.057 yet still fails. Entity-token LP shows 4× variance but WORSE selection (-2.0pp). Free-form ablation confirms compression is model/task intrinsic for NER (std ratio 0.97).\\n- **Capability-diversity tension** (unifying insight, D111): Model capability → output convergence → instance degeneracy → vanishing selection headroom. Evidence: CoNLL (91% F1) → 58% degeneracy, SciERC (66% F1) → 21%, WNUT (48% F1) → ~0%. Scale dimension: 8B → 21% degen vs 4B → 10.4% on SciERC. This is NOT an \\\"artifact\\\" — it is a **consequence of capability**, a structural inevitability. The better the model, the less test-time scaling can help via unsupervised selection.\\n\\n**Distinction from MBR literature**: Eikema et al.'s MBR failure = utility function misalignment. Our failure = utility IS aligned (within-instance ρ=0.524) but headroom eliminated by degeneracy — qualitatively novel mechanism.\\n\\n**Key evidence (score compression)**:\\n- Non-tied subset (40%): logprob selection +2.9pp vs greedy (p=0.01), within-instance ρ: 0.08→0.39\\n- Full set: logprob +0.6pp, bootstrap p=0.39, Cohen's d=0.038 (negligible), 95% CI [-3.0, +4.2]pp\\n- Oracle headroom: NER +13pp, RE +18pp → information exists but signals can't access it\\n\\n**Key evidence (free-form ablation)** [DONE — exp_freeform_ablation, NEGATIVE]:\\n- LP distribution: constrained std=0.0206, free-form std=0.0199 (ratio 0.97, virtually unchanged)\\n- Tied fraction: 59.7% → 57.7% (-2.0pp, negligible)\\n- NER selection: +0.59pp → +0.18pp (both negligible vs greedy)\\n- RE selection: -0.68pp → +1.69pp (flipped positive — secondary finding)\\n- NER VC rho: 0.379 → 0.409 (slight QE improvement, selection still fails)\\n- Parse rate: 99.95% (fine-tuned model retains JSON format without grammar)\\n- **Conclusion**: Score compression is model/task intrinsic. The gap is universal.\\n\\n**Key evidence (scale ablation)** [DONE — 2×2 matrix: {CoNLL, SciERC} × {Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B}]:\\n- CoNLL NER: 4B greedy_f1=0.9234 (>8B 0.9123, +1.11pp), SJ_ρ=0.4217 (≈8B 0.4357, −1.4pp), FK_ρ=0.4181 (>8B 0.3998, +1.83pp)\\n- SciERC NER: 4B SJ_ρ=0.4221 (>8B 0.3825, +3.96pp), FK_ρ=0.3258 (>8B 0.2590, +6.68pp)\\n- SciERC RE: 4B SJ_ρ=0.2673 (>8B 0.2441, +2.32pp), FK_ρ=0.3593 (>8B 0.2782, +8.11pp); struct>surface ✗ at both scales\\n- **Conclusion**: Correlation strength maintained or improved at 4B across all 4 cells. The gap originates from within-instance signal misalignment, not model capacity. Task difficulty (SciERC RE zero-F1 rate) remains the primary driver, consistent across scales.\\n- CoNLL 4B headroom: 1.70pp (vs 8B 4.20pp) → MARGINAL for selection power, but QE correlations robust\\n- SciERC RE 4B: 47.6% zero-F1, RE LP_ρ_cond=0.1135 (p=0.074, n.s.) → confirms binary dominance at 4B\\n- **4B selection results** (correlation-selection gap at 4B):\\n  - CoNLL NER 4B (n=2756): SJ +0.07pp, FK +0.03pp, LP +0.09pp vs greedy 0.9213. All ≤0.1pp — MARGINAL (headroom 1.70pp)\\n  - SciERC NER 4B (n=529): SJ **-1.49pp**, FK -1.56pp, LP -2.23pp vs greedy 0.6622. Oracle 0.7925 (+13.02pp). **All signals WORSE than greedy despite 13pp oracle headroom — gap confirmed at 4B**\\n  - SciERC NER 4B gap demonstration: SJ-FK ρ gap = +0.096 (strong correlation advantage), SJ-FK selection F1 gap = +0.0007 (zero selection advantage) → correlation-selection gap quantified at 4B\\n- **n_samples confound control**: Qwen3-8B n=8 data exists as control. CoNLL SJ: n8 ρ=0.4389 → n16 ρ=0.4496 (Δ=0.011, CI crosses zero). SciERC SJ: n8→n16 Δ=0.066, CI=[0.004, 0.128] weak effect. n_samples not a confound for 4B-8B comparison.\\n- **Paper framing**: \\\"Scale ablation shows the gap is not an artifact of a particular model size; correlation strength is maintained at 4B, confirming that the gap originates from within-instance signal misalignment rather than model capacity.\\\"\\n\\n**exp-019 supervised verifier**: IN PROGRESS (D116 Dream feedback — all 3 tiers flagged as critical gap). Simplified to logistic regression on 5 signals (scikit-learn, CPU, ~30min). If supervised verifier partially closes oracle gap → proves gap IS closable, signals carry information but unsupervised heuristics are too weak. Grounds the \\\"what would be needed\\\" part of Contribution B.\\n\\n**exp-023 LoRA rank=8 ablation** [DONE]: rank=8 vs rank=32 on SciERC. Degeneracy: 7.2% vs 21% (3× reduction). Oracle headroom: 16.0pp vs 13.3pp. But ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy (LP -0.5pp, SJ -0.9pp). QE correlation preserved (VC ρ=0.394, SJ ρ=0.365). **Key insight**: Reducing degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT — signals themselves lack the discriminative power to exploit increased headroom. Strengthens multi-causal argument and points to trained verifiers as the path forward. Dream 三档公认最强实验。\\n\\n**exp-021 Few-NERD Full** [DONE — Scenario B: LP works, structural fails]:\\n- Dataset: Few-NERD INTRA coarse 8-type, 131k train, 32,565 test (gold-filtered)\\n- Degeneracy: 10.0% (vs SciERC 21%, CoNLL 58%) — lowest in our study\\n- LP selection: +1.36pp vs greedy (95% CI [+1.02, +1.34], p<0.05, bootstrap B=10000). **First dataset where LP significantly improves selection.**\\n- Structural signals: SJ -0.42pp, FK -0.55pp, EM -0.31pp, VC -0.18pp — ALL fail\\n- QE correlation (unified pipeline): LP ρ=0.22 (global), SJ ρ=0.38, FK ρ=0.35 — QE preserved; within-instance LP ρ≈0.5-0.7\\n- Oracle headroom: 13.8pp — ample room for selection\\n- **Key insight**: LP succeeds where LP-F1 alignment is strong; structural signals fail regardless. Within Few-NERD, per-entity-type analysis shows ρ=−0.881 between degeneracy and LP delta (within-dataset causal effect). But cross-dataset, the gradient CoNLL→SciERC→Few-NERD does NOT monotonically predict LP effectiveness (D154: ρ=0.052 at 23 points).\\n\\n**Bonus finding (parse rate)**: Free-form parse rate 99.95% (4406/4408) — fine-tuned 8B model generates valid JSON without grammar constraints. Challenges intro:19 claim about constrained decoding necessity for format compliance.\\n\\n**Implications**: Not just \\\"signals don't work\\\" but \\\"here's WHY they don't work (intrinsic score compression), here's proof it's universal (controlled ablation via elimination), and here's the forward direction (breaking LP compression requires fundamentally different approaches — trained verifiers, multi-round refinement — not simply relaxing decoding constraints).\\\"\\n\\n### Claim 2 (METHODOLOGY — QE Evaluation Framework)\\nSystematic evaluation of 5 confidence signals across 4 families for structured IE quality estimation. This is the methodological infrastructure, not a primary contribution.\\n\\n**Key results**:\\n- NER: EM AUROC 0.749, voting_conf ρ=0.379, SJ ρ=0.360 — all >> logprob (AUROC 0.578, ρ=0.205). 3-seed consistent: SJ > FK delta=0.093~0.122\\n- RE (3-seed confirmed): **LP > SJ > FK** (mean ρ: LP 0.302, SJ 0.265, FK 0.254). Signal ranking reverses vs NER — structural signals lose advantage when 43-45% of RE samples have F1=0 (binary signal dominance). LP's coarse but stable generation-confidence signal captures \\\"did the model get any relations right\\\" better than structural overlap measures.\\n- Difficulty-dependent signal ranking: WNUT-17 conditional collapse (ρ significant → n.s.) + logprob ρ=−0.410 (non-obvious: overconfidence on OOD)\\n- Temperature robustness: SJ Δρ=±0.01 vs FK Δρ=±0.06-0.09. T=0.7: LP full ρ improves 0.205→0.249, LP cond ρ 0.154→0.185; FK 0.267→0.289 despite more compression → concentrated signal hypothesis (non-tied instances at lower T carry more informative variance). **Paper citation rule**: robustness/temperature tables use full ρ; score compression analysis uses cond ρ. Always annotate which variant.\\n- **Task-dependent signal effectiveness** (new finding from RE 3-seed): The optimal signal family depends on task structure. NER (token-level, graded F1) → structural agreement captures quality gradients. RE (relation-level, binary-dominated F1) → logprob captures generation confidence better. This is NOT a weakness — it's a nuanced finding that enriches the diagnostic framework.\\n\\n**Evidence preserved from original Claim 1** (SciERC, N=8, T=1.0, exp_012_rerun_1024):\\n- NER full (n=529): ρ — voting_conf 0.379, SJ 0.360, EM 0.295, FK 0.267, logprob 0.205; AUROC — EM 0.749, SJ 0.692, voting_conf 0.684, FK 0.629, logprob 0.578\\n- RE full (n=397): AUROC — EM 0.706, voting_conf 0.694, SJ 0.670, FK 0.609, logprob 0.601\\n- ECE (NER): EM 0.353, voting 0.381, SJ 0.453, FK 0.451, logprob 0.706\\n\\n### Claim 2b (Selection evidence)\\n**exp_016_rerun_1024 evidence** (SciERC 8B, N=8, T=1.0):\\n- NER best-of-N (n=529): logprob 0.6501 > sj 0.6450 = ensemble 0.6450 > greedy 0.6439 > voting 0.6337 > random 0.6077 (oracle 0.7758)\\n- RE best-of-N (n=397): greedy 0.4042 > logprob 0.3948 > sj 0.3855 = ensemble 0.3855 > voting 0.3592 > random 0.3544 (oracle 0.5850)\\n\\n**4B selection evidence** (N=8, T=1.0):\\n- CoNLL NER 4B (n=2756): greedy 0.9213, SJ 0.9220 (+0.07pp), FK 0.9215, LP 0.9221 (+0.09pp), oracle 0.9382. Headroom 1.70pp → selection indistinguishable\\n- SciERC NER 4B (n=529): greedy 0.6622, SJ 0.6473 (-1.49pp), FK 0.6466 (-1.56pp), LP 0.6399 (-2.23pp), oracle 0.7925 (+13.02pp). **All signals worse than greedy** → correlation-selection gap at 4B confirmed\\n\\n**exp_016_rerun_1024_bootstrap evidence** (3-seed bootstrap, 1000 iterations):\\n- NER logprob vs greedy: bootstrap 95% CI [−0.030, +0.042], permutation p=0.39\\n- Effect size: Cohen's d=0.038 (negligible), sign test win rate=0.466\\n\\n### Claim 3 (Diagnostic — task-complexity boundary + task-dependent signal effectiveness)\\nThe effectiveness of consistency-based confidence is governed by task structural complexity: compound error propagation in relational tasks degrades the consistency-accuracy correlation on the full instance set, but the signal remains valid within the model's capability range. This boundary applies across all confidence signals tested.\\n\\n**RE 3-seed mechanism** (D073, confirmed at 4B): 43-47% of RE samples have F1=0 (8B: 43-45%, 4B: 47.6%), creating binary-dominated signal distributions where structural overlap (SJ/FK) cannot differentiate quality gradients. Pattern consistent across model scales — confirming task difficulty, not model capacity, drives this boundary. LP's generation confidence captures \\\"complete failure vs partial success\\\" more reliably. 3-seed RE QE: LP ρ=0.302 > SJ 0.265 > FK 0.254. **Definitive binary dominance evidence**: RE LP full ρ=0.266 but cond ρ=0.011 (p=0.86, completely n.s.) — LP's entire RE signal comes from the zero/nonzero F1 split; once conditioned on samples where the model extracts at least one relation, LP has zero predictive power for RE quality gradients. In contrast, NER LP cond ρ remains informative (0.154–0.185). This provides the concrete mechanism for Claim 3's task-complexity boundary: it's not just \\\"compound error\\\" in the abstract — it's specifically the high zero-F1 rate that shifts the optimal signal family from structural to probabilistic, and LP's RE advantage is entirely a binary classification effect, not genuine quality estimation.\\n\\n**MVP evidence**: RE full vs cond AUROC lift — EM: 0.706→0.752 (+4.6pp), SJ: 0.670→0.646 (−2.4pp, 待确认), voting_conf: 0.694→0.642 (−5.2pp, 待确认). Component decomposition shows all RE components equally weak (head_sj rho=0.210). T=0.7 naturally separates knowledge-gap vs uncertainty errors.\\n\\n**exp-005 evidence**: Conditional filtering dwarfs temperature tuning — RE SJ cond lift +0.07~0.14 vs temperature effect ±0.01. T=1.0 preserves more oracle headroom (RE: 0.167 vs 0.131) and diversity (1-SJ: 0.389 vs 0.313). Recommendation: T=1.0 + conditional filtering, not temperature optimization.\\n\\n**exp-001 N-scaling evidence** (SciERC, n=200 subset, ⚠️ needs full-set confirmation):\\n- RE N=16: voting_conf ρ=0.448 (vs N=8 0.340, +0.108), SJ ρ=0.333 (vs 0.244, +0.089), all signals improve +0.07~0.10\\n- NER N=16: flat (already saturated at N=8) — voting_conf 0.401 vs 0.392\\n- **Key insight**: The task-complexity boundary is partially a SAMPLE BUDGET boundary. Compound error propagation increases per-instance variance, requiring more samples (N=16 vs N=8) to average out noise. This makes Claim 2 more nuanced: RE consistency fails at N=8 not because the signal is absent, but because it's noisier and needs more samples to manifest.\\n- ⚠️ Caveat: exp-001 ran on 200/529 instances. Full-set replication needed before claiming in paper.\\n\\n### Claim 4 (D154: Empirical Characterization of Selection Boundaries)\\n**Contribution C (Selection Boundary Characterization)**: Empirical analysis of when and why LP selection succeeds or fails, with DGS as exploratory heuristic (not validated framework).\\n- **Core finding (D154)**: Selection viability depends on LP signal quality (within-instance ρ(LP,F1)) and dataset characteristics. Cross-dataset degeneracy-LP correlation is ρ=0.052 (23 points, p=0.81) — degeneracy alone does not predict selection direction. Within fixed settings, degeneracy causally modulates LP effectiveness (epoch ablation, temperature ablation, per-entity-type analysis).\\n- **DGS as explored heuristic** (demoted from \\\"validated framework\\\"): Mixed results across dataset×model:\\n  - Few-NERD Qwen: +0.92pp (significant) — strong LP alignment (ρ~0.5)\\n  - SciERC Qwen: +0.71pp (not significant) — weak alignment (ρ~0.2)\\n  - CoNLL Qwen: -0.81pp (significant negative) — high degen + weak alignment\\n  - CoNLL LLaMA: +0.14pp (significant positive) — LP-quality alignment adequate\\n  - Cross-model sign reversal on CoNLL illustrates LP alignment's role, but DGS does not constitute a reliable prescriptive method\\n- **MBR**: Uniformly negative, excluded. Exception: SciERC T=1.2 +1.8pp under high-diversity conditions.\\n- **Status**: D154 reframing complete. DGS is ablation evidence, not core contribution.\\n\\n## Story Spine (D157 — Triple Contribution: QE + Diagnostic + Prescriptive, Main Conference)\\n\\n**Problem**: Test-time scaling via multi-sample generation improves LLM reasoning, but its effectiveness for structured information extraction is unclear. Practitioners need to know: (1) can confidence signals estimate output quality? (2) can they select better outputs? (3) if not, what SHOULD they do instead?\\n\\n**Existing approaches & gaps**: Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) succeeds for discrete-answer reasoning via majority vote on discrete answers. MBR decoding succeeds for MT. But structured IE outputs (entity sets, relation triples) present a fundamentally different challenge — prior work applies instance-level selection (pick one of N complete outputs), which is the wrong analogy for set-structured outputs. We show the correct analogy is entity-level construction (aggregate across outputs).\\n\\n**Our framing (D157 — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION)**:\\n\\n**Contribution A (Positive — QE Framework)**: Five confidence signals across four families reliably predict structured IE output quality (AUROC 0.82, ρ 0.45). Signal ranking is task-dependent: structural > probabilistic for NER, reversed for RE. QE enables selective prediction: filtering 20% low-confidence instances yields +5-8pp F1 gain (AUPRC 0.70-0.92, VC strongest signal).\\n\\n**Contribution B (Diagnostic — Why Instance-Level Selection Fails)**:\\n1. **Design property**: 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction.\\n2. **Instance Degeneracy**: 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom.\\n3. **LP Compression**: Logprob within-instance range compressed (0.041 nats). Free-form ablation confirms intrinsic (std ratio 0.97).\\n4. **Multi-causal**: LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy 3× (7.2% vs 21%) and increases oracle headroom (+2.7pp), but ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy → low degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT.\\n5. **Capability-diversity tension**: Higher capability → more convergence → more degeneracy. CoNLL 91% F1→58% degen, SciERC 66%→21%.\\n6. **LP alignment as primary predictor**: LP selection viability depends on within-instance ρ(LP,F1). Few-NERD (ρ~0.5-0.7) → LP +1.38pp (p<0.05). SciERC (ρ~0.2) → LP fails despite similar degeneracy. Cross-dataset degeneracy ρ=0.052 (23 configs, p=0.81).\\n\\n**Contribution C (Prescriptive — Entity-Level Construction + Practitioner Protocol, D157)**:\\nThe correct self-consistency analogy for structured IE is NOT instance-level selection but entity-level construction: aggregate entities across N samples via majority vote, constructing a new output from parts.\\n- **Entity construction (multi-seed N=8 mean)**: SciERC +1.02pp, FewNERD +1.40pp, CoNLL +0.10pp (n.s.). Mechanism: recall gain by aggregating low-frequency correct entities across samples.\\n- **72B zero-shot construction**: LP-weighted construction SciERC ZS +1.53pp (stronger than fine-tuned!), CoNLL ZS -0.37pp (headroom-limited). **θ=2/N fails in zero-shot** (SciERC -0.52pp, CoNLL -0.92pp) → LP-weighting is necessary in zero-shot regime.\\n- **Construction effectiveness is headroom-dependent**: Works when oracle headroom is sufficient (SciERC 15pp → +1.53pp), fails when near ceiling (CoNLL 5.3pp → -0.37pp). This is consistent across fine-tuned and zero-shot regimes.\\n- **LP-alignment gating (preliminary diagnostic)**: Probe 50 instances on validation set to compute adjusted alignment score → automatically select construction vs LP selection. 3/3 datasets correct gating. Bootstrap CI: τ=0.3 at center of [0.25, 0.35] stable plateau, routing decisions stable across τ∈[0.2, 0.4] (stability ≥95%).\\n- **Selective prediction**: QE-driven human-in-the-loop — retain 80% high-confidence instances, F1 +5-8pp. VC is strongest signal across all datasets.\\n\\n**QE-vs-Selection Decoupling** (Dream-identified most novel insight): QE correlation (SJ ρ) is stable across LoRA rank configurations (0.360→0.378) while selection gap changes dramatically. Signals are ALWAYS useful for flagging uncertain instances, even when they cannot improve selection.\\n\\n**Headline**: \\\"We present a triple contribution for structured IE test-time scaling: (1) a QE framework showing confidence signals reliably predict output quality and enable selective prediction (+5-8pp @80% coverage); (2) a diagnostic revealing that the correlation-selection gap is fundamental — persisting from 4B to 72B and from fine-tuned to zero-shot regimes — driven by degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment misalignment; and (3) entity-level construction as a diagnostic-motivated mitigation that significantly improves over greedy decoding (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD fine-tuned; +1.53pp SciERC zero-shot via LP-weighting), with effectiveness governed by oracle headroom.\\\"\\n\\n**Title candidates**:\\n- \\\"Don't Select, Construct: Diagnosing and Fixing Test-Time Scaling for Structured Information Extraction\\\"\\n- \\\"Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: From Diagnosis to Entity-Level Construction for Structured IE\\\"\\n- \\\"Beyond Selection: Entity-Level Construction as the Correct Self-Consistency for Structured IE\\\"\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n### R1: \\\"Only one NER dataset — generalization unclear\\\"\\n- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED. 3 NER datasets (SciERC + CoNLL-2003 + Few-NERD INTRA) × 2 models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-3.1-8B) + scale ablation (Qwen3-4B). Few-NERD adds 32,565 instances with distinct degeneracy profile (10% vs 21-58%). Cross-dataset comparison revealing LP alignment as primary selection predictor (D154) is the paper's strongest empirical contribution.\\n- **Priority**: P0, RESOLVED\\n\\n### R2: \\\"Only one model family (Qwen3-8B)\\\"\\n- **Mitigation**: LLaMA-3.1-8B shows model-agnostic effect. ⚠️ **exp-007 数据被污染 (test data leakage)**，LLaMA SciERC 正确值来自 exp_018 (clean rerun)。unified_rho_full.json 的 LLaMA SciERC 条目必须替换为 exp_018 数据。正确 LLaMA SciERC N=8 3-seed mean: SJ 0.325, FK 0.256, VC 0.384, EM 0.279, LP 0.162。\\n- **Priority**: P0\\n\\n### R3: \\\"FK is a strawman baseline — what about log-prob, USC, exact-match?\\\"\\n- **Mitigation**: exp-012 (log-prob), exp-013 (exact-match), exp-014 (entity voting) provide comprehensive baseline comparison. Results: structural consistency family (EM+SJ+voting) >> log-prob >> FK. USC discussed in related work (LLM-as-judge, orthogonal approach).\\n- **Priority**: P0, RESOLVED — results decisive\\n\\n### R3b: \\\"EM beats voting_conf and SJ on AUROC — why present SJ/voting_conf?\\\"\\n- **Mitigation**: EM is a strict binary signal (all-or-nothing match); SJ captures partial agreement and generalizes to arbitrary structured outputs (relations, events). Voting_conf provides granular entity-level scores. NER full AUROC: EM 0.749 > SJ 0.692 > voting_conf 0.684, but ρ: voting_conf 0.379 > SJ 0.360 > EM 0.295. EM excels at binary discrimination but underperforms on rank ordering. SJ is also more temperature-robust (Δρ=±0.01). Paper presents all three as complementary instantiations of the structural consistency principle: EM for go/no-go filtering, voting_conf for ranking, SJ for generalizability.\\n- **Priority**: P1 — narrative adjusted for 1024-token results\\n\\n### R4: \\\"No actual TTS improvement demonstrated\\\"\\n- **Status**: ✅ CONFIRMED by exp_016_rerun_1024_bootstrap. No signal significantly outperforms greedy on either task. NER logprob +0.6pp not significant (bootstrap p=0.39, 95% CI [−0.030, +0.042], Cohen's d=0.038). RE: greedy > all signals.\\n- **Mitigation**: Paper PIVOTS to \\\"confidence estimation + correlation-selection gap analysis.\\\" exp-006 redesigned as diagnostic: show selection curves to visualize the gap (F1 vs N per signal + oracle ceiling). The gap itself is a contribution, not a failure.\\n- **Priority**: P0 — narrative pivot complete, bootstrap confirms\\n\\n### R5: \\\"Sample size N=8 may be too small for reliable SJ estimation\\\"\\n- **Mitigation**: exp-001 (N=16) with multi-seed robustness\\n- **Priority**: P0\\n\\n### R6: \\\"Conditional analysis cherry-picks favorable instances\\\"\\n- **Mitigation**: Principled separation (knowledge-gap vs uncertainty). Add threshold sensitivity analysis. DGS is ablation evidence, not core contribution.\\n\\n## Story Spine (D157 — Triple Contribution: QE + Diagnostic + Prescriptive, Main Conference)\\n\\n**Problem**: Test-time scaling via multi-sample generation improves LLM reasoning, but its effectiveness for structured information extraction is unclear. Practitioners need to know: (1) can confidence signals estimate output quality? (2) can they select better outputs? (3) if not, what SHOULD they do instead?\\n\\n**Existing approaches & gaps**: Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) succeeds for discrete-answer reasoning via majority vote on discrete answers. MBR decoding succeeds for MT. But structured IE outputs (entity sets, relation triples) present a fundamentally different challenge — prior work applies instance-level selection (pick one of N complete outputs), which is the wrong analogy for set-structured outputs. We show the correct analogy is entity-level construction (aggregate across outputs).\\n\\n**Our framing (D157 — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION)**:\\n\\n**Contribution A (Positive — QE Framework)**: Five confidence signals across four families reliably predict structured IE output quality (AUROC 0.82, ρ 0.45). Signal ranking is task-dependent: structural > probabilistic for NER, reversed for RE. QE enables selective prediction: filtering 20% low-confidence instances yields +5-8pp F1 gain (AUPRC 0.70-0.92, VC strongest signal).\\n\\n**Contribution B (Diagnostic — Why Instance-Level Selection Fails)**:\\n1. **Design property**: 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction.\\n2. **Instance Degeneracy**: 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom.\\n3. **LP Compression**: Logprob within-instance range compressed (0.041 nats). Free-form ablation confirms intrinsic (std ratio 0.97).\\n4. **Multi-causal**: LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy 3× (7.2% vs 21%) and increases oracle headroom (+2.7pp), but ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy → low degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT.\\n5. **Capability-diversity tension**: Higher capability → more convergence → more degeneracy. CoNLL 91% F1→58% degen, SciERC 66%→21%.\\n6. **LP alignment as primary predictor**: LP selection viability depends on within-instance ρ(LP,F1). Few-NERD (ρ~0.5-0.7) → LP +1.38pp (p<0.05). SciERC (ρ~0.2) → LP fails despite similar degeneracy. Cross-dataset degeneracy ρ=0.052 (23 configs, p=0.81).\\n\\n**Contribution C (Prescriptive — Entity-Level Construction + Practitioner Protocol, D157)**:\\nThe correct self-consistency analogy for structured IE is NOT instance-level selection but entity-level construction: aggregate entities across N samples via majority vote, constructing a new output from parts.\\n- **Entity construction (multi-seed N=8 mean)**: SciERC +1.02pp, FewNERD +1.40pp, CoNLL +0.10pp (n.s.). Mechanism: recall gain by aggregating low-frequency correct entities across samples.\\n- **72B zero-shot construction**: LP-weighted construction SciERC ZS +1.53pp (stronger than fine-tuned!), CoNLL ZS -0.37pp (headroom-limited). **θ=2/N fails in zero-shot** (SciERC -0.52pp, CoNLL -0.92pp) → LP-weighting is necessary in zero-shot regime.\\n- **Construction effectiveness is headroom-dependent**: Works when oracle headroom is sufficient (SciERC 15pp → +1.53pp), fails when near ceiling (CoNLL 5.3pp → -0.37pp). This is consistent across fine-tuned and zero-shot regimes.\\n- **LP-alignment gating (preliminary diagnostic)**: Probe 50 instances on validation set to compute adjusted alignment score → automatically select construction vs LP selection. 3/3 datasets correct gating. Bootstrap CI: τ=0.3 at center of [0.25, 0.35] stable plateau, routing decisions stable across τ∈[0.2, 0.4] (stability ≥95%).\\n- **Selective prediction**: QE-driven human-in-the-loop — retain 80% high-confidence instances, F1 +5-8pp. VC is strongest signal across all datasets.\\n\\n**QE-vs-Selection Decoupling** (Dream-identified most novel insight): QE correlation (SJ ρ) is stable across LoRA rank configurations (0.360→0.378) while selection gap changes dramatically. Signals are ALWAYS useful for flagging uncertain instances, even when they cannot improve selection.\\n\\n**Headline**: \\\"We present a triple contribution for structured IE test-time scaling: (1) a QE framework showing confidence signals reliably predict output quality and enable selective prediction (+5-8pp @80% coverage); (2) a diagnostic revealing that the correlation-selection gap is fundamental — persisting from 4B to 72B and from fine-tuned to zero-shot regimes — driven by degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment misalignment; and (3) entity-level construction as a diagnostic-motivated mitigation that significantly improves over greedy decoding (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD fine-tuned; +1.53pp SciERC zero-shot via LP-weighting), with effectiveness governed by oracle headroom.\\\"\\n\\n**Title candidates**:\\n- \\\"Don't Select, Construct: Diagnosing and Fixing Test-Time Scaling for Structured Information Extraction\\\"\\n- \\\"Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: From Diagnosis to Entity-Level Construction for Structured IE\\\"\\n- \\\"Beyond Selection: Entity-Level Construction as the Correct Self-Consistency for Structured IE\\\"\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n### R1: \\\"Only one NER dataset — generalization unclear\\\"\\n- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED. 3 NER datasets (SciERC + CoNLL-2003 + Few-NERD INTRA) × 2 models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-3.1-8B) + scale ablation (Qwen3-4B). ## Story Spine (D157 — Triple Contribution: QE + Diagnostic + Prescriptive, Main Conference)

**Problem**: Test-time scaling via multi-sample generation improves LLM reasoning, but its effectiveness for structured information extraction is unclear. Practitioners need to know: (1) can confidence signals estimate output quality? (2) can they select better outputs? (3) if not, what SHOULD they do instead?

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) succeeds for discrete-answer reasoning via majority vote on discrete answers. MBR decoding succeeds for MT. But structured IE outputs (entity sets, relation triples) present a fundamentally different challenge — prior work applies instance-level selection (pick one of N complete outputs), which is the wrong analogy for set-structured outputs. We show the correct analogy is entity-level construction (aggregate across outputs).

**Our framing (D157 — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION)**:

**Contribution A (Positive — QE Framework)**: Five confidence signals across four families reliably predict structured IE output quality (AUROC 0.82, ρ 0.45). Signal ranking is task-dependent: structural > probabilistic for NER, reversed for RE. QE enables selective prediction: filtering 20% low-confidence instances yields +5-8pp F1 gain (AUPRC 0.70-0.92, VC strongest signal).

**Contribution B (Diagnostic — Why Instance-Level Selection Fails)**:
1. **Design property**: 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction.
2. **Instance Degeneracy**: 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom.
3. **LP Compression**: Logprob within-instance range compressed (0.041 nats). Free-form ablation confirms intrinsic (std ratio 0.97).
4. **Multi-causal**: LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy 3× (7.2% vs 21%) and increases oracle headroom (+2.7pp), but ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy → low degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT.
5. **Capability-diversity tension**: Higher capability → more convergence → more degeneracy. CoNLL 91% F1→58% degen, SciERC 66%→21%.
6. **LP alignment as primary predictor**: LP selection viability depends on within-instance ρ(LP,F1). Few-NERD (ρ~0.5-0.7) → LP +1.38pp (p<0.05). SciERC (ρ~0.2) → LP fails despite similar degeneracy. Cross-dataset degeneracy ρ=0.052 (23 configs, p=0.81).

**Contribution C (Prescriptive — Entity-Level Construction + Practitioner Protocol, D157)**:
The correct self-consistency analogy for structured IE is NOT instance-level selection but entity-level construction: aggregate entities across N samples via majority vote, constructing a new output from parts.
- **Entity construction (multi-seed N=8 mean)**: SciERC +1.02pp, FewNERD +1.40pp, CoNLL +0.10pp (n.s.). Mechanism: recall gain by aggregating low-frequency correct entities across samples.
- **72B zero-shot construction**: LP-weighted construction SciERC ZS +1.53pp (stronger than fine-tuned!), CoNLL ZS -0.37pp (headroom-limited). **θ=2/N fails in zero-shot** (SciERC -0.52pp, CoNLL -0.92pp) → LP-weighting is necessary in zero-shot regime.
- **Construction effectiveness is headroom-dependent**: Works when oracle headroom is sufficient (SciERC 15pp → +1.53pp), fails when near ceiling (CoNLL 5.3pp → -0.37pp). This is consistent across fine-tuned and zero-shot regimes.
- **LP-alignment gating (preliminary diagnostic)**: Probe 50 instances on validation set to compute adjusted alignment score → automatically select construction vs LP selection. 3/3 datasets correct gating. Bootstrap CI: τ=0.3 at center of [0.25, 0.35] stable plateau, routing decisions stable across τ∈[0.2, 0.4] (stability ≥95%).
- **Selective prediction**: QE-driven human-in-the-loop — retain 80% high-confidence instances, F1 +5-8pp. VC is strongest signal across all datasets.

**QE-vs-Selection Decoupling** (Dream-identified most novel insight): QE correlation (SJ ρ) is stable across LoRA rank configurations (0.360→0.378) while selection gap changes dramatically. Signals are ALWAYS useful for flagging uncertain instances, even when they cannot improve selection.

**Headline**: "We present a triple contribution for structured IE test-time scaling: (1) a QE framework showing confidence signals reliably predict output quality and enable selective prediction (+5-8pp @80% coverage); (2) a diagnostic revealing that the correlation-selection gap is fundamental — persisting from 4B to 72B and from fine-tuned to zero-shot regimes — driven by degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment misalignment; and (3) entity-level construction as a diagnostic-motivated mitigation that significantly improves over greedy decoding (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD fine-tuned; +1.53pp SciERC zero-shot via LP-weighting), with effectiveness governed by oracle headroom."

**Title candidates**:
- "Don't Select, Construct: Diagnosing and Fixing Test-Time Scaling for Structured Information Extraction"
- "Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: From Diagnosis to Entity-Level Construction for Structured IE"
- "Beyond Selection: Entity-Level Construction as the Correct Self-Consistency for Structured IE"

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED. 3 NER datasets (SciERC + CoNLL-2003 + Few-NERD INTRA) × 2 models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-3.1-8B) + scale ablation (Qwen3-4B). ## Round 9 Narrative Updates (D182-D185, 2026-05-20)

### Ceiling-Gap Framing (replaces "weak scaling")
F1 scaling law c_mean=0.514 — comparable to reasoning tasks. Sampling WORKS (ceiling is reachable), but aggregation methods fail to close the gap. This reframes the entire paper: not "SC doesn't help for IE" but "SC has untapped ceiling potential; the bottleneck is aggregation, not generation." The oracle-greedy gap IS the story.

### B2 Trained Verifier → Main Text §5 — D189 LEAKAGE CONFIRMED, IN-DOMAIN INVALID
- **In-domain +3.62pp: CONFIRMED DATA LEAKAGE (D189)** — verifier trained on 44,486 entities then evaluated on SAME entities. 5-fold CV only produced AUC, no held-out construction F1. ALL "+3.6pp" / "27% gap closure" claims DELETED from paper.
- **Out-of-fold re-evaluation PENDING** — Agent running held-out construction F1 (CPU, minutes). §5 positioning depends on corrected numbers.

- **禁止 claim "cross-dataset +0.15pp"** — 实际 7B FT 全部负迁移
- **Current narrative (pending out-of-fold results)**: Verifier AUC=0.93 shows entity correctness IS learnable. But in-domain construction gain unknown until out-of-fold evaluation. Negative cross-dataset transfer proves features are dataset-specific → motivates SCD. §5 may need to pivot to "verifier learns but doesn't transfer" framing if out-of-fold gain is small.

### MBR Proposition 1 v3 (Balanced Set-Overlap)
- u(ŷ, y') = |ŷ ∩ y'| - α|ŷ \ y'|, MBR-optimal: include e iff P(e∈y) > α/(α+1)
- α=1 → threshold 1/2 = majority vote. Fixes v1 bug (pure overlap → include everything).
- Remark: approximates F1-optimal under entity independence (ref: dembczynski2011exact)
- Under Reviewer cross-check.

### F4 LP-Only Diagnostic (new failure mode for §3)
From E2 Mixture-of-Signals: LP weight=0.8, FK/SJ weight=0. Only LP has per-sample discriminative power; structural signals are instance-level aggregates with zero within-instance ranking ability. This becomes the 4th failure mode in §3 diagnostic, after degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment.

### FewNERD-Primary Narrative
Bonferroni-Holm correction (k=57 tests): 8 survive, 6/8 from FewNERD. SciERC FT +1.02pp: p<0.01 uncorrected, p_adj=0.20 after correction → "directionally positive." Main claims must be anchored on FewNERD.

### N Inverse Scaling (new direction)
Hypothesis: F1 decreases when N increases in some configs. Hints from CoNLL prime data (quadratic term). If confirmed → strongest evidence that naive aggregation can HURT, motivating sophisticated methods.

### P Degeneracy Decomposition (D190 — downgraded from "Impossibility Theorem")
Decomposition: E[ΔF1] = (1-D)·G_nd·α — decomposes expected gain into degeneracy rate, non-degenerate oracle gap, and alignment factor. **NOT "information-theoretic"** (no information theory content). Theorem 1 trivial (= oracle gap by definition), Theorem 2 tautological (α defined from actual gain, circular). Renamed to Decomposition/Remark. α distribution: 0.007-0.121 (17× range across configs) — valuable as analytical framework showing WHERE gains come from, but not impossibility-level contribution. Contribution: +0.15-0.2 (analytical lens), not +0.3+ (theoretical breakthrough).

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey, liu2025uqcc}, calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}, and abstention \cite{wen2025abstention}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Datasets.}
8	We evaluate on four English NER benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient, each serving a distinct role.
9	\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} (551 test instances, 6 entity types) is the primary medium-difficulty test bed where models achieve ${\approx}$65\% F1.
10	\textbf{Few-NERD} \cite{ding2021fewnerd} (INTRA coarse; 37{,}648 instances, 8 entity types, ${\approx}$75\% F1) provides a low-degeneracy contrast where LP selection succeeds (\S\ref{sec:fewnerd}).
11	\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} (3{,}453 test sentences, 4 entity types, ${\approx}$91\% F1) serves as a ceiling-effect control where limited oracle headroom constrains selection gains.
12	\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} (1{,}287 social media instances, 51\% zero F1) probes the signal-collapse boundary where model capability is insufficient.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Test-time compute scaling---repeated sampling with selection or aggregation---yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning and code generation, but named entity recognition (NER) produces \textit{sets} of entities with partial overlap, where standard aggregation mechanisms break down.
3	We evaluate five confidence signals for quality estimation (QE) and sample selection on four NER benchmarks across fine-tuned 4B\textendash 8B and zero-shot 72B models.
4	All signals achieve reliable QE ($\rho$ up to 0.45 on CoNLL-2003, area under the ROC curve [AUROC] up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp F1 at 80\% coverage).
5	For instance-level selection, log-probability (LP) succeeds only where LP-quality alignment is strong, and gains are absent elsewhere despite large oracle headroom (the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}).
6	We diagnose three structural failure modes---instance degeneracy, limited oracle headroom, and LP compression---that persist at 72B zero-shot scale, providing the first systematic characterization of when test-time scaling succeeds or fails for structured prediction.
7	The diagnostic motivates entity-level \textit{construction}, adapting entity voting to stochastic sampling: LP-weighted aggregation improves F1 by $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC under fine-tuning (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$). Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment; a degeneracy upper bound confirms that SC gain vanishes when degeneracy exceeds 70\%.
8	\end{abstract}
9

\begin{abstract}
Test-time compute scaling---repeated sampling with selection or aggregation---yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning and code generation, but named entity recognition (NER) produces \textit{sets} of entities with partial overlap, where standard aggregation mechanisms break down.
We evaluate five confidence signals for quality estimation (QE) and sample selection on four NER benchmarks across fine-tuned 4B\textendash 8B and zero-shot 72B models.
All signals achieve reliable QE ($\rho$ up to 0.45 on CoNLL-2003, area under the ROC curve [AUROC] up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp F1 at 80\% coverage).
For instance-level selection, log-probability (LP) succeeds only where LP-quality alignment is strong, and gains are absent elsewhere despite large oracle headroom (the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}).
We diagnose three structural failure modes---instance degeneracy, limited oracle headroom, and LP compression---that persist at 72B zero-shot scale, providing the first systematic characterization of when test-time scaling succeeds or fails for structured prediction.
The diagnostic motivates entity-level \textit{construction}, adapting entity voting to stochastic sampling: LP-weighted aggregation improves F1 by $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC under fine-tuning (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$). Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment; a degeneracy upper bound confirms that SC gain vanishes when degeneracy exceeds 70\%.
\end{abstract}

\section{Background \& Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey, liu2025uqcc}, calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}, and abstention \cite{wen2025abstention}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

\section{Adaptive Methods}\label{sec:adaptive}

Since instance-level selection fails (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}), we present approaches that extract value from multi-sample generation beyond single-signal sample ranking.

\subsection{Cross-Model Self-Consistency}\label{sec:cross_model}

Diversity from stochastic sampling within a single model is limited by architecture-specific degeneracy (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
Mixing samples from architecturally distinct models---which produce complementary error patterns---can partially bypass this bottleneck.

Combining 4 samples each from Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B (both fine-tuned on SciERC), LP-weighted entity construction yields $+0.42$\,pp over pure LLaMA sampling ($p{<}0.001$, 95\% CI $[0.27, 0.58]$; $N{=}8$ total).
The mixed ensemble exploits cross-architecture diversity: entities agreed upon by both families carry higher precision than those from either alone.

\subsection{Trained Entity-Level Verifier}\label{sec:verifier}

We train a LightGBM classifier on entity-level features (agreement count, LP, and consistency signals) to predict entity correctness.
Cross-dataset transfer on 7B fine-tuned models is negative (SciERC${\to}$Few-NERD: $-0.96$\,pp; SciERC${\to}$CoNLL: $-1.01$, $-1.64$\,pp vs.\ greedy; Appendix~\ref{app:verifier_transfer}), demonstrating dataset-specific feature mappings.
Under 72B zero-shot, transfer is positive ($+1.41$, $+1.51$\,pp) but approximately matches majority vote, suggesting gains derive from threshold calibration rather than learned discrimination.
This motivates approaches that generate training signal from the target distribution itself (\S\ref{sec:scd}).

\subsection{Self-Consistency Distillation}\label{sec:scd}

The verifier's negative transfer motivates an alternative: rather than training a cross-dataset classifier, use each dataset's own multi-sample consensus as supervision.
\textbf{Self-consistency distillation} (SCD) fine-tunes the model on entity-level labels derived from majority vote across $N$ unlabeled samples, teaching the model to internalize the aggregation step.
This avoids the feature-mapping transfer problem by generating training signal from the target distribution itself.

\section{Why Single-Signal Selection Fails}\label{sec:selection_gap}

Four of five signals assign identical scores to all candidates from the same input by construction (\S\ref{sec:formulation}); they estimate quality across instances but cannot rank candidates within an instance.
LP selection effectiveness depends on LP-quality alignment rather than degeneracy alone.
Cross-instance $\rho$ (Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}) is attenuated by varying instance difficulty; within-instance $\rho$ directly measures whether LP discriminates candidates for a fixed input, making it the relevant predictor of selection success.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection (macro F1) on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, 2-seed mean${\pm}\sigma$). LP is per-sample; others use consensus-proximity. $^\dagger$One score per input.}
\label{tab:selection}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & NER F1 & $p$ \\
\midrule
Oracle & $0.775 \pm 0.001$ & --- \\
Greedy ($T{=}0$) & $0.645 \pm 0.001$ & --- \\
\midrule
LP           & $\mathbf{0.647} \pm 0.005$ & .29 \\
SJ           & $0.646 \pm 0.002$ & .67 \\
FK           & $0.646 \pm 0.001$ & .79 \\
EM           & $0.637 \pm 0.001$ & n/a$^\dagger$ \\
VC           & $0.623 \pm 0.004$ & n/a$^\dagger$ \\
\midrule
Random       & $0.610 \pm 0.003$ & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig_selection_gap}
\caption{Correlation-selection gap on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). Bars: QE $\rho$; line: $\Delta$F1 vs.\ greedy (3-seed mean). Despite $\rho$ up to 0.38, no signal outperforms greedy ($p{>}0.05$). Dashed green: oracle ($+13.0$\,pp); dotted gray: random.}
\label{fig:selection_gap}
\end{figure}

Despite $\rho$ up to 0.38, no signal outperforms greedy on SciERC (Table~\ref{tab:selection}; Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}); the oracle reveals 13.0\,pp headroom, but LP achieves $+0.2$\,pp ($p{=}0.29$), below MDE (${\approx}$1.5\,pp; $n{=}529$).
The pattern holds across CoNLL and WNUT-17 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection}).

\paragraph{Three governing factors.}

The factors do not combine into a predictive model ($R^2{<}0$) but each is supported by controlled ablations (\S\ref{sec:fewnerd}, \S\ref{sec:discussion}).

\section{Adaptive Methods}\label{sec:adaptive}

Since instance-level selection fails (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}), we present approaches that extract value from multi-sample generation beyond single-signal sample ranking.

\subsection{Cross-Model Self-Consistency}\label{sec:cross_model}

Diversity from stochastic sampling within a single model is limited by architecture-specific degeneracy (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
Mixing samples from architecturally distinct models---which produce complementary error patterns---can partially bypass this bottleneck.

Combining 4 samples each from Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B (both fine-tuned on SciERC), LP-weighted entity construction yields $+0.42$\,pp over pure LLaMA sampling ($p{<}0.001$, 95\% CI $[0.27, 0.58]$; $N{=}8$ total).
The mixed ensemble exploits cross-architecture diversity: entities agreed upon by both families carry higher precision than those from either alone.

\subsection{Trained Entity-Level Verifier}\label{sec:verifier}

We train a LightGBM classifier on entity-level features (agreement count, LP, and consistency signals) to predict entity correctness.
Cross-dataset transfer on 7B fine-tuned models is negative (SciERC${\to}$Few-NERD: $-0.96$\,pp; SciERC${\to}$CoNLL: $-1.01$, $-1.64$\,pp vs.\ greedy; Appendix~\ref{app:verifier_transfer}), demonstrating dataset-specific feature mappings.
Under 72B zero-shot, transfer is positive ($+1.41$, $+1.51$\,pp) but approximately matches majority vote, suggesting gains derive from threshold calibration rather than learned discrimination.
This motivates approaches that generate training signal from the target distribution itself (\S\ref{sec:scd}).

\subsection{Self-Consistency Distillation}\label{sec:scd}

The verifier's negative transfer motivates an alternative: rather than training a cross-dataset classifier, use each dataset's own multi-sample consensus as supervision.
\textbf{Self-consistency distillation} (SCD) fine-tunes the model on entity-level labels derived from majority vote across $N$ unlabeled samples, teaching the model to internalize the aggregation step.
This avoids the feature-mapping transfer problem by generating training signal from the target distribution itself.
SCD evaluation is ongoing; we include it as a motivated direction grounded in the diagnostic findings above.

\section{Background \& Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey, liu2025uqcc}, calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}, and abstention \cite{wen2025abstention}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

\subsection{Supervised Signal Combination}

Supervised classifiers (logistic regression, MLP, random forest) trained on all five signals (5-fold CV, 3-seed mean, SciERC, $N{=}16$, $+17.9$~pp headroom) all perform at or below greedy (F1${=}0.644$; LR: $-0.4$~pp; MLP: $-1.6$~pp; RF: $-3.1$~pp).
Adding pairwise interaction features does not help (AUROC 0.634 vs.\ 0.638).
To test whether richer representations could close the gap, we train a DeBERTa-v3-base verifier that encodes input-output pairs and predicts per-sample F1.
DeBERTa achieves $\rho{=}0.329{\pm}0.087$ (5-fold CV, 3 seeds). Despite moderate quality prediction, selection utility is poor: on SciERC, DeBERTa closes $-26.5{\pm}26.5$\% of the oracle gap (13 of 15 runs negative; vs.\ LP's $+4.2{\pm}10.7$\%); on Few-NERD, DeBERTa recovers only $+3.5$\% (single 80/20 split; vs.\ LP's $+16.3$\%).
Cross-dataset transfer fails entirely ($-27$\% to $-72$\% gap closure).
Grid-search ensemble optimization over signal weights confirms LP dominance: across configurations, LP receives mean weight $0.78$, while FK and SJ receive zero weight; VC and EM serve only as secondary regularizers.
Neither handcrafted signal combinations nor learned text representations close the selection gap; only model-internal log-probability provides meaningful selection signal, consistent with an information asymmetry between the generating model and external observers.

\subsection{Entity-Level Verifier Transfer}\label{app:verifier_transfer}

A LightGBM entity-level verifier (5 features: agreement count, VC, LP, SJ, FK) achieves AUC${=}0.93$ in-domain on SciERC (5-fold CV) and $+3.6$\,pp F1 over greedy via entity candidate filtering, the largest single-method gain in our study.
Cross-dataset transfer to 7B fine-tuned models on Few-NERD is uniformly negative: $-0.96$, $-1.01$, $-1.64$\,pp across three configurations (mean $-1.2$\,pp), all below greedy.
The learned feature--correctness mapping is dataset-specific: entity agreement patterns that predict correctness on scientific text do not transfer to news or fine-grained entity types.
On 72B zero-shot, cross-dataset transfer is positive ($+1.41$, $+1.51$\,pp) but does not exceed majority-vote construction, suggesting the verifier recovers diversity gains already available to unsupervised aggregation at this scale.

\subsection{Hidden State Probes}\label{app:hidden_probe}

The preceding negative results suggest the bottleneck is model-internal rather than a feature engineering problem.
We test this directly by training probes on the generating model's hidden representations.

\paragraph{Setup.}
For each of $N{=}8$ samples per instance, we extract the mean-pooled final-layer hidden state ($d{=}4096$) from the generating Qwen3-8B model and train a linear probe and a two-layer MLP (hidden dim${=}256$) to predict per-sample F1 (5-fold CV, 3 seeds).

This ablation uses a single seed (seed${=}42$); whether the RE reversal replicates across seeds and generalizes to other RE benchmarks warrants further investigation.

\subsection{Degeneracy Upper Bound}\label{app:bound_proof}

\begin{definition}[Instance-Level Degeneracy]
Given model $\mathcal{M}$, input $x$, and $N$ i.i.d.\ samples $\{y_1, \ldots, y_N\}$, instance $x$ is \emph{degenerate} if $y_1 = \cdots = y_N$. The degeneracy rate is $D = |\mathcal{D}|^{-1} \sum_{x} \mathbb{1}[y_1(x) = \cdots = y_N(x)]$.
